title: Network Programming (I)
subtopics: socket concept and types (stream, datagram, raw)
socket primitives: socket(), bind(), listen(), accept(), connect()
data transfer: send(), recv(), read(), write()
byte-order functions: htons(), htonl(), ntohs(), ntohl()
address conversion: inet_aton(), inet_ntoa(), inet_pton(), inet_ntop()

definitions.definition: An endpoint for communication between two programs over a network
Berkeley Software Distribution socket API – standard for network programming in C
Associates a socket with a local address and port
Marks a socket as passive – ready to accept connections
Accepts an incoming connection on a listening socket
Initiates a connection to a remote server
Big-endian (network byte order) vs little-endian (host byte order)

learning_objectives: Use the BSD socket API to create TCP client and server programs
Correctly handle byte order and address structures
